rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Path 1/2/3 taxonomy is named in chunk 1 (lines 11-13) and every later reuse re-states the mechanism, not just the number — chunk 2 line 23 '`gh` CLI (Path 3, first-party CLI)', line 32 '(Path 1, connector inheritance, or Path 2, `claude mcp add`)'; chunk 3 line 60 references 3LO which is defined in the same parenthetical it appears in; chunk 6 line 93 '(Path 2)' — all resolve under sequential-deck-read (arc-earned within this single file, rule-1 NOT-violation). Closest borderline: chunk 4 line 77 'Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path.' — 'the three trackers' resolves against GitHub Issues/Jira/Linear headers already read (chunks 2-4), 'path' resolves against the Path-N vocabulary reused earlier in the same chunk (line 70). Line 5's 'the maintainer `Source verification` block' points past the `<!-- maintainer -->` cut but names a real block rather than locating it by position, and every reader-facing chunk's own referents close inside chunks 1-8. No never-named or vague-with-full-history instance found in any of the 9 chunks.

No callback to another curriculum file anywhere in the body; every outbound doc-level pointer is an external citation URL with descriptive link text. Chunk 1 line 15 now reads 'Per-tracker install commands come next. Plugins distribute Path 2, `claude mcp add`, at scale, under *Plugins and marketplaces*.' (confirmed against the diff since e11bbeb4: the prior 'on this page' page-position tail was removed) — names the target section by its real title, satisfying 'name it, don't locate it', and 'come next' is a reading-order pointer within the carve-out.

Every chunk carries a self-sufficient claim. Shortest chunk (5, 'Other trackers', lines 83-88) still has two full sentences plus a Sources line: 'Check the Anthropic Directory for reviewed connectors and your tracker's own docs. Most have a third-party MCP or a CLI fallback (like `gh`).' — not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked all 8 body headers against their own chunk content. Line 104 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' is answered inside the same chunk: official-vs-team marketplaces (line 106), enterprise pre-registration (line 108), a plugin-vs-`claude mcp add` decision rule (line 110) — the header's three clauses each map to a paragraph the reader is holding. Line 21 '## GitHub Issues' is answered by the whole chunk covering issue/PR/Action workflows via `gh` and the GitHub MCP server — not contradicted by its own content.

`grep -nE '\bNot [A-Za-z].*\. *Not [A-Za-z]' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md` -> 0 matches (no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'). Manual scan of all 9 chunks found no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no number+own-retraction pattern, no abstraction-noun stacks, no verb triplets with an empty leg. Self-grading-superlative sub-item checked specifically: closest line is chunk 4 line 77 'Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path.' — this grades an external product (Linear) against two other external products (Jira, GitHub) named in the same file, not the training's own exercises or moves, so it is not the value-prop-leak shape §7 bans (`check_writing.md §13`); it stays inside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -noE '\bsurface\b|\bbeat\b|\bcompendium\b|\bforcing function\b|\bmood\b|Connections\b' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md` inside the body region (lines 1-123): 'surface' at line 30 ('The surface is broad: every GitHub REST/GraphQL endpoint is reachable via `gh api`') — ordinary engineering sense ('API surface'), not the repo's meta-dialect ('writing surface'); covered by §8's own audience-register carve-out. 'beat' at line 110 ('When plugins beat `claude mcp add`.') — ordinary-English verb 'outperform', a different part of speech from the curriculum's noun jargon for a narrative beat; no engineer in the room parses it as the latter. 'compendium', 'forcing function', 'mood' and 'Connections' do not appear in the body at all (their only hits are inside the `<!-- maintainer -->` cut, out of §8's scope by construction).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file lives in `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/` and opens 'Flat lookup' (line 1), so it is a lookup surface: the per-slide bold-count budget is off, the ≲5-word handle cap still binds. Scanned every `**...**` span in the body with backtick-code stripped before counting (replicating `check-slide-size.js`'s word-count approach): 29 spans total, all but two are ≤5 words (single-word term defs, 'Sources:', 'Easiest path: Claude.ai inheritance.', etc.). The two over cap are lines 12 (7w, 'Path 2, `claude mcp add` from the command line.') and 13 (6w, 'Path 3, first-party CLI via Bash.') — the file's own Path-1/2/3 taxonomy, a coined term reused verbatim at lines 23, 32, 34, 40, 60(3LO context), 93, 110; bolding the full descriptive tag rather than the bare number keeps the handle legible as the thing later chunks cite back to, which is the 'coined term' bold-purpose the rule lists, not a narrative sentence. Confirmed the previously-flagged narrative violation is fixed: line 60 ('individual engineers don't need per-install admin approval') carries no bold span at all in the current body (verified in the same scan) — the diff since pin e11bbeb4 removed it.

This is the fix for the 2026-07-09 incident rule 10 warns about (reference pages silently dropped from the deck); the current renderer code includes them. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <this file>` independently confirms all 8 body `##` sections are enumerated by the same composed-deck walk ('files: 1 slides: 8'), so nothing here is stranded outside the deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet/list item and every chunk's closing sentence against the three classes. (a) Doctrine restatement: the Path 1/2/3 taxonomy (lines 11-13) and the 'Current gaps' bullets (lines 118-120) each add a distinct move or object (a different install mechanism; a different missing feature) rather than re-announcing a split already stated. (b) Self-referential design commentary: none anywhere — flat technical lookup page, zero pedagogy-of-the-training language. (c) Aphorism kicker: no chunk closes on a koan restating its own header; closest candidate, chunk 7 line 110's closing clause 'For a one-off solo install on one machine, plain Path 1 or Path 2 stays simpler.' stays inside because it is a concrete decision rule (which path, and when), not a restatement of the header 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution'.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15's grammar split is stated only for exercise headings (imperative/phase label) vs lecture headings (claims) -- this file is a reference page, a third file type the rule text doesn't address. Checked anyway for fit: all 8 headings, including the new split 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' (line 104), are noun-phrase topic/catalogue labels naming their subject (explicit NOT-violation carve-out even if the rule did apply), consistent with the lookup-surface register the compendium describes at §9.
